//Secrets: Jwt:Key and Customers:ClientFingerprintKey below are DEVELOPMENT-ONLY values, and they are
here rather than in User Secrets for exactly one reason: so `dotnet run` works on a fresh
clone with no setup step. They are not secrets — anyone reading this repository has them,
which is the definition of a value that protects nothing.
Note what is deliberately NOT done: appsettings.json carries no key at all. Production
therefore FAILS TO START unless the environment or a key vault supplies one, because
JwtOptions.Validate() and CustomersOptions.Validate() both throw on a missing value. A
convenient fallback in the base file would have been one line shorter and would have meant
a deployment silently running on a key published on the internet.
Onyx S5 is the alternative: appsettings.json, committed, holding a live payment gateway API
key, a production database password and the JWT signing key, with no environment-specific
override anywhere. Its PR noted that the config 'has the real values in it so it works out
To override locally without touching this file:
dotnet user-secrets set "Jwt:Key" "<a long random string>"
//Sales: Every interval here is cut down for development so the recovery layers are observable in a
single session rather than inferred from the code. The production defaults in SalesOptions
are 1 minute / 30 minutes / 1 hour grace / 15 minutes.
OrphanGracePeriod stays comfortably longer than CheckoutSession.Lifetime even here: the
orphan sweep releases stock, and a grace period shorter than the checkout lifetime would
have it competing with live customers for the stock they are legitimately holding.
//PaymentGateway: UseStub runs the whole payment flow without a provider account. PaymentGatewayOptions
refuses it outside Development, and the process fails to START if it is set there: a stub
gateway in production approves every payment, which is exactly the observable behaviour
The stub is driven by the token, so every branch is reachable by hand:
tok_decline      a definitive decline (insufficient_funds). Never retried.
tok_expired      a decline with expired_card, to see the message change.
tok_timeout      INDETERMINATE. The stub really does charge; the caller never learns.
Watch the payment sit unresolved, then watch payments.reconciliation
ask the provider and resolve it to Captured. This is Onyx M5.
tok_unreachable  a transport failure. The provider never saw it.
tok_noref        success with no reference. The payment must NOT settle (M4).
ApiKey and WebhookSecret are DEVELOPMENT-ONLY values, here so `dotnet run` works on a
fresh clone. They are not secrets — anyone reading this repository has them. Note that
appsettings.json carries no PaymentGateway section at all, so production FAILS TO START
without one. Onyx S5 committed a LIVE payment gateway key to appsettings.json.
//NotificationSender: UseLogging writes every notification to the application log instead of sending it, so the
whole chain - event, consumer, enqueue, claim, send, delivery record - runs on a fresh
clone with no provider account. The roadmap asks for this specifically: Onyx A32 is a CSV
import that was implemented, tested, advertised in the README, and called by nothing but
the test project. A notification path that only works once somebody configures a provider
NotificationSenderOptions refuses it outside Development, and the process FAILS TO START
if it is set there: a sender that records every message as delivered and transmits nothing
is Onyx A8 - 'no customer has ever received any communication from this system' - reached
deliberately. The delivery log records which sender handled each attempt, which is how such
a mistake would be noticed anyway.
Bodies that contain a token are REDACTED in the log. Putting messages where a developer can
read them is what makes this sender useful and exactly what would put live password-reset
links into an aggregated log file. Read the real link from
GET /api/notifications/{id} inside the retention window, or from the database.
//Observability: Spans go to the Aspire dashboard from docker-compose.observability.yml:
then open http://localhost:18888 and pick Traces. See docs/OBSERVABILITY.md.
SampleRatio is 1 here because the point of a development run is to watch one specific
flow, and a sampled-out trace is indistinguishable from a broken one. It is applied
parent-based in every environment, so turning it down never cuts a flow in half at the
Nothing listening on 4317 is not an error: the exporter retries and gives up, and the
application behaves identically. Set Enabled to false to switch instrumentation off
entirely, in which case ActivitySource.StartActivity returns null everywhere and outbox
rows are written with null trace columns and delivered exactly as before.
